name: Mitch Green

positions.statement: On his campaign website, Green says he is fighting for lower utility bills for everyday Portlanders.
positions.excerpt: lower utility bills for everyday Portlanders

positions.statement: On his campaign priorities page, Green lists universal healthcare among the things he fights for.
positions.excerpt: fight for truly affordable housing, universal healthcare, tenant protections

positions.statement: On his campaign priorities page, Green says his climate approach means ditching fossil fuels and banning data centers.
positions.excerpt: That means ditching fossil fuels, banning data centers

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says he sponsored an ordinance reestablishing the Fair Wage Code (January 15, 2025).
On his campaign record page, Green says he secured funding to restart an independent evaluation of Portland Street Response in the FY 25-26 budget.
positions.excerpt: Mitch secured funding to restart an independent evaluation of Portland Street Response.

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says he led a May 8, 2025 resolution to build $200 million of new sidewalks in Districts 1 and 4.
positions.excerpt: a resolution to build $200 million of new sidewalks in Districts 1 and 4

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says he was tear-gassed at the Labor Against ICE Rally on January 31, 2026 while standing up against federal violence.
positions.excerpt: Mitch was tear-gassed while standing up against federal violence at the Labor Against ICE Rally.

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says he coordinated the expedited relocation of Cottonwood School in summer 2025.
positions.excerpt: Mitch coordinated the expedited relocation of Cottonwood School

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green is described as a strong supporter of Preschool for All who pledged to defend the program.
positions.excerpt: A strong supporter of Preschool for All, Mitch pledged to defend the program

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says an ordinance he and Councilor Morillo sponsored banning AI rent-setting algorithms passed on November 19, 2025.
positions.excerpt: passed an ordinance banning predatory AI rent-setting algorithms on November 19, 2025

positions.statement: On his campaign record page, Green says he has called out the administration's attacks on free speech.
positions.excerpt: calling out the administration's attacks on free speech.

positions.statement: On his campaign priorities page, Green says it is time to end backroom deals at City Hall.
positions.excerpt: It's time to end backroom deals at City Hall.

positions.statement: On his campaign website, Green lists cost controls for projects such as Bull Run among his priorities.
positions.excerpt: cost controls for runaway projects like Bull Run

positions.statement: In a May 14, 2026 council office release, Green said his Care Package amendments aim to move away from forced displacement of homeless Portlanders into overnight shelters.
positions.excerpt: the failed approach of forced displacement of homeless Portlanders into overnight shelters.

source.publisher: City of Portland, Councilor Green's office

positions.statement: In his December 14, 2025 year-one recap on the City of Portland site, Green wrote that he called on fellow veterans to reject illegal and immoral orders.
positions.excerpt: I called on my fellow veterans to reject illegal and immoral orders and to stand against rising fascism.

source.publisher: City of Portland, Councilor Green's office

voting_record.statement: Willamette Week reported in a September 2026 correction that Green opposed a council measure authorizing additional debt for Bull Run upgrades, along with Councilor Morillo and Council President Dunphy.
voting_record.excerpt: That measure was opposed by councilors Angelita Morillo and Mitch Green and Council President Jamie Dunphy.
